records.name: Gideon
records.held_by: The Gideon civic council in the old Governor's Mansion, over a Lukiul Argonian majority with Nibenese-descended families
records.summary: Gideon is the western frontier city of Black Marsh, built on the dry road through a flooded hillscape and on the Ayleid ruins of Twyllbek. In 4E 201 it keeps a courthouse and a civic council in the old Governor's Mansion, and it openly denies the Archwardens' claim to rule it.

notes.text: Gideon is the first settlement on the Blackwood Road from Leyawiin: a governor's mansion, a courthouse, a Temple of Dibella, an arena and mud bathhouses in a maze of cramped streets. Most buildings stand along Blackwood Way because it is the only dry ground through the town.

Barsaebic Ayleids founded it as Twyllbek; the Kothringi left a Dibella devotion in the soil; Imperial settlers built the mansion, the temple and Castle Giovesse beside it. The An-Xileel's weapon killed the Lukiul majority in 4E 48 and the undead host of Umbriel overran the town, yet Gideon's destruction was light and it stayed an active settlement.

In 4E 201 the council still sits in the Governor's Mansion and the courthouse still hears cases and keeps its records, the one Imperial habit the town never dropped. Gideon denies the successor state's claim and deals with the Archwardens only at Fort Silvermoth's toll gate. Carts on the Blackwood Road to Leyawiin leave from the east gate.

Most people are Lukiul Argonians who speak Cyrodiilic, trade with outsiders and stand apart from Argonian philosophy, beside Nibenese-descended families two centuries settled. Archein families survive as landholders and council servants. About 90 people live in the walls; Khajiit and Bosmer traders pass through.

Hunting produce, herbs, red-clay pottery from the Onkobra delta and the Leyawiin trade keep the market busy, and the cooks serve outsiders swamp food they can stomach. River boats bring Middle Argonian goods down to the quay, and salt and iron go out to the Naka-Desh river stations.

Dibella is worshipped openly in the old Dorcia Martius manor, a devotion the Nibenese took from the Kothringi substrate; Sithis is honoured in private by the Argonians. The Hist garden holds a planted cutting whose ownership is disputed.

Imperial brick and timber along Blackwood Way, wet red clay underfoot, crooked alleys running off the causeway, and Ayleid white-stone stumps in the plaza and the southern gardens. Steam rises from the bathhouses and fog lies in the streets at dawn.
The town is guarded and safe by day. The closed Ayleid sections, the Ruction Ring's cut-throats and the swamp at the gates (death hoppers, fleshflies, hackwings) are where visitors get hurt.

A Hist cutting in the Ayleid gardens that two families both claim, a cellar door in the closed Ayleid quarter that someone has forced, a Kothringi silver mask sold twice in one week, and the old quarrel with Soulrest over who ships the bay's trade.

notes.text: Calyphe was a Dibella shrine of the Kothringi at the western end of the mangrove country, a few miles from the Gideon road. When the Knahaten Flu emptied the Blackwood in 2E 560 its keepers died untended, and the mangroves have grown through the floor since.
The shrine is unheld. Diggers from Gideon reach it by flat-bottomed boat through the mangrove channels, and Naka-Desh boatmen tie a chime to the roots at the landing on their way past.
The shrine is uninhabited. A Nibenese shrine-seeker from Gideon may leave an offering at the altar slab. The diggers keep a camp on the dry hummock beside it.
It was a place of offerings, not of trade. Now the leaf-carved stone is prised out and carried to Gideon, and small gold and silver votives still turn up in the root-mud round the altar.

The altar slab is Dibella's, and the leaf-and-wave carving on it is the Kothringi sign of her. Gideon's Nibenese bring flowers and wine to it, and the Naka-Desh hang tin chimes in the mangroves above.
Leaf-carved grey stone sunk to the lintels in black mud, with mangrove roots arched over the altar and the broken pillars. Chimes tick in the branches over it.
Mangrove crocodiles and mudcrabs lie in the channel at the landing, and the pools round the altar are deep enough to drown in. Gideon's diggers say ghost lights at dusk lead the careless into them.

notes.text: Mnemosa is a burial terrace of the Kothringi on the high ground of Nha Enasa, east of Gideon. The terrace was filled at the height of the Flu in 2E 560, so the stones carry far more names than the settlement ever had.

No one holds it. The Naka-Desh treat it as a place to be visited, not lived in and paddle up from the channels to renew their chimes. Diggers who rob the terraces are driven off if the river-folk catch them.
The terrace is uninhabited. Naka-Desh come in pairs at the turn of the year to tend the chime-posts. Now and then a grave-robber from Gideon is found in the reeds.
The terrace was the Kothringi's burial ground, so it never traded. Now it draws grave-robbers after the burial goods. The Naka-Desh keep it as a place of memory.

Each grave is marked with a stone and a chime-post, and the Kothringi hung tin and copper chimes there to speak to the dead. The Naka-Desh, friends of the Kothringi in life, keep the ring of posts in repair.
Stepped terraces of grave-stones set in a ring of weathered chime-posts, with the posts hung with green-crusted tin and copper. Reeds have taken the lowest step and a shallow pool sits in the middle.
The dead of the terrace stir at night and the pool is deep with leeches. Naka-Desh watchers will shoot at a looter who disturbs the graves.

notes.text: Pelaxis was the Kothringi river quay and boat-house on the channel east of Gideon, where shallow-draft sail-and-paddle boats were built and repaired. When the Flu emptied it in 2E 560, the last boat was left half-planked on the slip.
The quay is unheld. A few Naka-Desh river-folk beach their boats against the old mooring stones, and diggers from Gideon come to see the abandoned slip.
The quay is uninhabited. Naka-Desh fishers sleep under the boat-house roof in bad weather. Boatwrights from Gideon visit now and then to look at the Kothringi hull design.
A boatyard on the river trade between Gideon and the interior. Now it is a source of ship-timber and iron fittings, and the one place where the old Kothringi boat design can still be seen.
The Kothringi hung a Kynareth wind-chime from the quay's end to ask for fair wind, and the Naka-Desh still cut a small notch on the mooring stone for a safe journey. Nothing grander is kept.
A stone quay with mooring posts sunk in the bank, a long boat-house with its roof half gone and a launching slip with a half-built hull still on it. Weed hangs from the quay edge.
The planking is rotten and the slip ends over deep water where slaughterfish feed. Crocodiles lie below the quay in the shade of the boat-house.

notes.text: A Paatru hunters' camp on the western edge of the Hist country: reed lean-tos on a riverbank, a smoke-rack and a drawn-up boat.

The Paatru hunt the forest edge west of the Hist country, and this bank is one of their old hunting grounds, left to them because the Naka-Desh fish the channels below and never wanted the dry reeds above. The interior tribes were untouched by Umbriel, so the camp has stood on the same bank for as long as the hunters remember.
A handful of Paatru hunters and an egg-tender keep the bank. The lean-tos stand all year, and there is always a hide on the rack.
Six Paatru: three hunters, an egg-tender, a hide-curer and a youth learning to net. They are wary of strangers who come by boat and warn them off by banging on a hollow log.
They hunt along the reeds and cure the hides on the rack for sale at Gul-Tej. The riverbank gives them fish and reed-grubs between the hunts.
They honour Sithis and the Hist of Low-Crown, and hang feather and reed charms from the smoke-rack. A tiny totem-stone by the landing is turned to face the water at dawn.
Lean-tos of reed and hide among tall reeds, a smoke-rack by the bank and a boat drawn up on the mud. The ground is trampled flat around a hearth pit.
Hunters on the bank challenge strangers within bow-range. Swamp crocodiles and snakes use the same reeds.

notes.text: Sarth-Hul Station is a stilt post deep in the Nha Enasa's reeds, where the Root-Folk of Helstrom tend a Hist sapling grown from a cutting of their forest trees. They planted it here so that hunters far from the great forest still have a tree to hatch under.
Four Saxhleel hold the post. They hunt and tend the sapling, and the tree-minders' boat comes from Helstrom to fetch sap and bring news.
Four Root-Folk: a sapling-tender, two hunters and an egg-sitter. They speak the root-talk of the great trees, and hold that visitors who lie to them are seen by the Hist.
They hunt the reeds for birds and eels, and send sap and egg-gifts to Helstrom. Little leaves the station except by the tree-minders' own boat.
The Hist sapling at the post's heart is sacred, and its whispers guide the keepers' choices. They hatch eggs under it and bury their dead in the reed-beds beside it.
A stilt platform in the reed-beds, with a drying rack, an egg-hut and a young Hist sapling with a ring of stones round it. The reeds are tall enough to hide the whole post.
The reeds hide crocodiles and snakes, and the keepers shoot at anyone who touches the sapling. Few outsiders can find the post.
An egg to protect, a Hist whisper to follow, or a hunter lost in the reeds.

Four Saxhleel keep the post and trade quietly with the basin tribes. They tend a clutch of eggs in the egg-hut and say little to anyone.
Four Root-Folk: an egg-tender, two hunters and a rack-keeper. They are watchful of the Mine-Burner tribes, who think of the basin as theirs.
They hunt and dry fish on the rack and sell it to the Mine-Burner watch posts. They send egg-gifts to Helstrom once a year.
They keep a clutch hearth in the egg-hut and carry hatchlings to a Hist when the eggs come. Their dead go back by boat to the tree they came from.
A stilt platform in the northern reeds with a long drying rack, an egg-hut with a thatch roof and a boat landing hidden in the grass. Smoke from the fish-rack hangs over it.
